 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The Utah Jazz will face the Los Angeles Lakers tonight in their second fixture of the season. The last time these two sides met, Luka Doncic dropped 52 points and fell just two rebounds short of a triple-double in a 132-123 Lakers win .
 Before the game, the Jazz head coach, Will Hardy , told the media about how the team prepared to stop Luka Doncic from going off tonight. Subsequently, he also shared his feelings about facing former Jazz player Walker Kessler .
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "I have written on my [white] board, 'Hope is not a strategy.' So that's out," Hardy said initially about how the Jazz prepared to defend Luka Doncic tonight.
 "It's hard because you go back and watch the film afterward, and it tests your ability to be critical of yourself. And also to recognize that in certain moments, we did a really good job, and he was just better." 
 "It's a psychological battle more than anything. Especially when he hits a couple of tough deep threes or throws a pass that maybe no one expected," he further added .
 Luka Doncic had 52 points, 10 assists, and eight rebounds in their last meeting with the Jazz, shooting 17-30 from the field (56.7% FG) and 8-18 from beyond the arc (44.4% 3P).
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The former Jazz player, Walker Kessler, had little impact in the first game (finishing with just two points and seven rebounds) but has since settled into his role with the Lakers.
 Will Hardy also shared his thoughts on facing him on the court tonight and whether he regrets not finding a place for him to stay with the Jazz.
 "I value my relationship with him and all the experiences we went through together…. There was a long-standing relationship there. Ultimately, I'm happy for Walker as a human being because we have a real relationship. He's a wonderful guy," said Hardy on his relationship with Walker Kessler.
 "As far as thinking about him being with us, those are sort of dangerous places to get into because you start going down an unproductive road. This is our group we are focused on helping. I always want the guys that we have relationships with to do well; tonight we're competing against him." 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "But the nature of our business has always been that way. It's something that we all adjust to. I saw Walker before the game, and it takes a second to recognize him in the Lakers' gear, but we're in it to compete tonight," Hardy concluded .
 Ultimately, Hardy knows containing Doncic will require more than simply executing a defensive game plan, especially after witnessing his brilliance firsthand.
 Meanwhile, facing a former player like Walker Kessler adds another layer to the matchup. But the Jazz coach appears determined to set emotions aside and focus on getting his team a win tonight amid their struggles this season.
 It remains to be seen if the Jazz (2-13) can end the Lakers' (13-2) nine-game winning streak tonight. All eyes will be on Luka Doncic and Walker Kessler's performance and how the Jazz can counter this two-man threat tonight in Austin Reaves' absence.
